The outer lip is thin, slightly arcuate, and smooth within, with a feeble varix behind it. The short siphonal canal is hardly differentiated from the aperture with a deep siphonal sulcus forming an evident fasciole. This species is distributed in the Pacific Ocean from Sonora, Mexico to Panama.

Estos caracoles son típicamente pequeños, alcanzando aproximadamente 2.5 cm de longitud. La concha se caracteriza por tener marcas espirales oscuras que se asemejan a puntos o guiones anchos. A. punctulata se distribuye a lo largo de la costa oeste de América del Norte, desde Monterey, California, hasta el norte de Baja California, México. Habitan en las zonas intermareales superiores de costas rocosas. La distancia de Procrustes indica que la forma de la concha es más divergente en comparación con otras en el grupo.

ficha_en: Conus nux, commonly known as the nut cone, is a species of sea snail in the family Conidae. These snails are predatory and venomous and can sting humans, thus live specimens should be handled carefully. The shell size varies between 10 mm and 26 mm. It is coronated with a rather depressed spire and is granular striate towards the base. The shell color is white, marbled with chestnut, and it may have obscure white bands near the upper part and below the middle of the body whorl. The base of the shell is tinged with violet. This species is found in the Pacific Ocean from Southwestern Baja California, Mexico, to Ecuador, including the Galápagos Islands.
ficha_es: Conus nux, conocido comúnmente como el cono de nuez, es una especie de caracol marino de la familia Conidae. Estos caracoles son depredadores y venenosos, y pueden picar a los humanos, por lo que los especímenes vivos deben manejarse con cuidado. El tamaño de la concha varía entre 10 mm y 26 mm. Está coronada con una espira bastante deprimida y es estriada granular hacia la base. El color de la concha es blanco, jaspeado con castaño, y puede tener bandas blancas en la parte superior y debajo de la mitad de la vuelta del cuerpo. La base de la concha está teñida de violeta. Esta especie se encuentra en el Océano Pacífico desde el suroeste de Baja California, México, hasta Ecuador, incluyendo las Islas Galápagos.

ficha_en: Conus purpurascens, commonly known as the purple cone, is a species of predatory and venomous sea snail belonging to the family Conidae. The shell varies in size from 33 mm to 80 mm, and exhibits a broad-shouldered shape with a striate spire. The shell texture is striate below the shoulder, sometimes slightly granular, and features clouded coloration of white or violaceous and brown or olive, with close chestnut and white minute articulations. Occasionally, it displays irregular white bands in the middle. The coloration is diverse yet the overall shell habit remains relatively consistent. Conus purpurascens is found in the Central Pacific, specifically around the Galapagos Islands and the Gulf of California in Mexico. With a Procrustes distance of 1238839, the species is morphologically divergent from the average shape typical of the genus Conus. Conantokin-P, a toxin useful in research, is derived from its venom, providing a unique ecological relationship with its environment and potential medical applications.
ficha_es: Conus purpurascens, conocido comúnmente como cono púrpura, es una especie de caracol marino depredador y venenoso perteneciente a la familia Conidae. El tamaño de la concha varía entre 33 mm y 80 mm, y presenta una forma de hombro amplio con una espira estriada. La textura de la concha es estriada debajo del hombro, a veces ligeramente granular, y muestra una coloración nublada de blanco o violáceo y marrón u oliva, con líneas articuladas finas de castaño y blanco. Ocasionalmente, se presentan bandas blancas irregulares en el medio. La coloración es diversa aunque el hábito general de la concha permanece bastante constante. Conus purpurascens se encuentra en el Pacífico Central, particularmente alrededor de las Islas Galápagos y el Golfo de California en México. Con una distancia de Procrustes de 1238839, la especie es morfológicamente divergente de la forma promedio típica del género Conus. El conantokin-P, una toxina útil en investigación, se deriva de su veneno, proporcionando una relación ecológica única con su entorno y posibles aplicaciones médicas.

ficha_en: Crepidula onyx is a species within the genus Crepidula, commonly referred to as slipper snails. The shells of these gastropods are characterized by their simple structure and plastic morphology, which can lead to challenges in taxonomy. Crepidula onyx has been noted to be morphologically divergent from its group average, with a Procrustes distance to the mean shape indicating a more atypical shell form. This species is well-studied for its role as an exotic invasive species in marine habitats. It falls within a group actively researched due to distinctive life history traits such as protandrous sex change, a process known to be environmentally mediated and influenced by interactions with other snails. Crepidula onyx shares its ecological and developmental research context with the related species, Crepidula fornicata, another well-studied invasive organism.

Crepidula onyx comparte su contexto de investigación ecológica y de desarrollo con la especie relacionada, Crepidula fornicata, otro organismo invasor bien estudiado.

Acanthinucella spirata is a species of predatory sea snail, a marine gastropod mollusk in the family Muricidae, commonly known as murex snails or rock snails. This species is distributed along the Pacific Ocean coast of North America, living predominantly in rocky intertidal zones.

The shell morphology of Acanthinucella spirata includes distinct forms, with some individuals exhibiting a morphological divergence from the average shape within the group, as indicated by a Procrustes distance to the mean shape. The species is predatory, feeding primarily on the genus Littorina, and employs paralytic venom to capture prey. Its reproductive strategy involves laying egg capsules that range in length from 4 to 9 mm, each containing 17 to 49 embryos.

Acanthinucella spirata was historically utilized by Native American groups such as the Chumash in Central California, around 1000 to 1200 AD. The species has been recorded to extend its range north of previously known distributions.

Su estrategia reproductiva implica la puesta de cápsulas de huevos que miden de 4 a 9 mm de largo, cada una conteniendo de 17 a 49 embriones.

Históricamente, Acanthinucella spirata fue utilizada por grupos nativos americanos como los chumash en el centro de California, alrededor del año 1000 al 1200 d.C. Se ha registrado que la especie ha extendido su rango al norte de las distribuciones previamente conocidas.

ficha_en: Alanbeuella corrugata, known as the 'gaudy frog shell', is a species of sea snail belonging to the family Bursidae, the frog shells. The maximum recorded shell length is 75 mm. The shell is ovate, somewhat depressed, and ponderous, with a chestnut color. The whorls are encircled by two or three rows of large, livid chestnut-colored pimples. The varices are granulously ridged. The columella is granulously wrinkled, characterized by white wrinkles, while the outer lip is flatly fimbriated, sinuated at the upper part, brown in color and radiated with whitish grooves. Alanbeuella corrugata is found at depths ranging from 2 m to 137 m in marine environments. Its geographic distribution extends across the Atlantic Ocean off West Africa, the Canary Islands, Cape Verdes, and Brazil; as well as the Caribbean Sea, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Lesser Antilles. The Procrustes distance for this species is 1228403, suggesting a highly divergent shell form from the group average, indicating atypical morphological characteristics within its genus.
ficha_es: Alanbeuella corrugata, conocida como 'concha de rana llamativa', es una especie de caracol marino perteneciente a la familia Bursidae, las conchas de rana. La columela está arrugada de manera granular, caracterizada por arrugas blancas, mientras que el borde exterior es franjado de forma plana, sinuado en la parte superior, de color marrón y con estrías blanquecinas radiadas. Alanbeuella corrugata se encuentra en profundidades que van desde los 2 m hasta los 137 m en ambientes marinos. Su distribución geográfica se extiende a través del Océano Atlántico frente a África Occidental, las Islas Canarias, Cabo Verde y Brasil; así como el Mar Caribe, el Golfo de México y las Antillas Menores. La distancia Procrustes para esta especie es 1228403, lo que sugiere una forma del caparazón altamente divergente del promedio del grupo, indicando características morfológicas atípicas dentro de su género.

ficha_en: The species Galeropsis monodonta, with synonyms giving its name as Coralliophila monodonta, is a marine gastropod mollusk belonging to the family Muricidae, also known as murex or rock snails. The shell size of this species ranges from 16 mm to 35 mm in height. The external color of the shell is off-white, while the interior displays a deep purple hue. It is naturally distributed in regions including Mozambique, New Zealand, Natal, and the Marquesas Islands, and has been introduced as an alien species in parts of the Adriatic Sea and Eastern Basin of the Mediterranean. The species typically inhabits coral-rich environments and possesses a shell morphology typical of the family Muricidae, which often features raised spirals and strong axial sculpture. Galeropsis monodonta shows a significant variance in shell form with a Procrustes distance of 1214544, indicating morphological divergence from the average shape within its group. Muricids are generally carnivorous, feeding on other marine organisms like gastropods, bivalves, and barnacles through predatory actions involving boring into prey shells. Reproduction involves laying eggs in protective capsules. The muricids have historical significance due to their role in producing Tyrian purple dye extracted from their shells.

El tamaño del caparazón de esta especie varía entre 16 mm y 35 mm de altura. El color exterior del caparazón es blanco sucio, mientras que el interior muestra un tono púrpura profundo. ficha_en: Littoraria varia is a species of sea snail within the family Littorinidae, commonly known as winkles or periwinkles. It is distributed from Panama to Peru. The genus Littoraria includes more than fifty species of marine gastropod mollusks, with many inhabiting the Tropical Eastern Pacific and thriving in mangrove forests above the high tide level. These snails typically feed on algae, epiphytes, fungi, diatoms, and the leaf epidermis of mangroves. The shell morphology of Littoraria species is often influenced by ecological factors, such as the height at which they live in mangroves, resulting in more variable shell color and thinner shells in higher elevations. Littoraria varia has notable morphological divergence from the mean shape within its group, given its high Procrustes distance. As a member of the Caenogastropoda subclass, it is classified under the order Littorinimorpha.

Estos caracoles generalmente se alimentan de algas, epífitas, hongos, diatomeas y la epidermis foliar de los manglares. La morfología de la concha de las especies Littoraria a menudo se ve influenciada por factores ecológicos, como la altura a la que viven en los manglares, resultando en un color de concha más variable y conchas más delgadas en elevaciones más altas. Glossaulax reclusiana, commonly known as Recluz's moon snail, is a species within the family Naticidae. The shell is ovate-conical and swollen, featuring a smooth or slightly striated surface. It is characterized by grayish-lead coloration, with the base being whitish and a distinctive dark band around the suture. The shell can reach up to 84 millimeters in height.
The umbilicus is large and mostly covered by a callus, which is unevenly divided by a groove. The columella is heavily calloused at the top, possessing a white upper part marked by a dark spot in the lower region. The ovate-semilunar aperture has a small channel at the top and is white to brownish inside.
G. reclusiana inhabits shallow bays and lagoons ranging from the intertidal zone to depths of approximately 49.5 meters along the coasts of California and Mexico. As a predatory species, it feeds primarily on other mollusks like Callianax biplicata and Chione fluctifraga.
This species exhibits a high Procrustes distance to the mean shape of its group, indicating it has a more divergent shell form compared to average morphological characteristics of related taxa.

Se caracteriza por un color grisáceo-plomo, con una base blanquecina y una distintiva banda oscura alrededor de la sutura. La concha puede alcanzar hasta 84 milímetros de altura.
El ombligo es grande y está mayormente cubierto por un callo, el cual está dividido de manera desigual por un surco. G. reclusiana habita en bahías y lagunas poco profundas que abarcan desde la zona intermareal hasta profundidades de aproximadamente 49.5 metros a lo largo de las costas de California y México. Como especie depredadora, se alimenta principalmente de otros moluscos como Callianax biplicata y Chione fluctifraga.
Esta especie exhibe una alta distancia de Procrustes al promedio de su grupo, indicando que presenta una forma de concha más divergente en comparación con las características morfológicas promedio de taxones relacionados.

ficha_en: Amphithalamus inclusus is a species of minute sea snails, marine gastropod mollusks or micromollusks belonging to the family Anabathridae. The shell of this species measures up to 1.1 mm in length and 0.9 mm in diameter. Its morphology resembles that of a small Stenothyra. The shell has a bluntly ribbed base and a cancellated nucleus, with the outer lip uncontracted and the columellar lip meeting forward in adults, leaving a chamber behind. The shell is pale brown, with an ashy tinge and a flesh-colored columellar region. The nuclear whorls count 1.5 with poorly developed spiral lirations. Post-nuclear whorls are strongly rounded, narrowly shouldered, with a weak peripheral keel and a sharply marked suture. The aperture is oval and greatly contracted by a shelf, characteristic of the genus. The operculum is thin and paucispiral. This species is found off the western coast of North America.

La concha de esta especie mide hasta 1.1 mm de longitud y 0.9 mm de diámetro. Su morfología se asemeja a la de un pequeño Stenothyra. La concha tiene una base con costillas romas y un núcleo cancelado, con el labio exterior no contraído y el labio columelar encontrándose hacia el frente en adultos, dejando una cámara detrás. La concha es de color marrón pálido, con un matiz ceniciento y una región columelar de color carne. Las vueltas nucleares cuentan 1.5 con liraciones espirales poco desarrolladas. Las vueltas postnucleares son fuertemente redondeadas, estrechamente hombreadas, con una quilla periférica débil y una sutura bien marcada. La abertura es ovalada y muy contraída por un estante, característico del género. El opérculo es delgado y paucispiral. Esta especie se encuentra frente a la costa occidental de América del Norte.

The species inhabits the cooler, temperate waters of the Eastern Pacific Ocean, ranging from the Farallon Islands near San Francisco to Bahía Magdalena in Baja California Sur, Mexico. In terms of feeding, the Californian cone is a generalist predator, hunting and consuming marine worms, fish, and other mollusks. It also exhibits scavenging behavior. Unique among its family, this species has diverging molecular (including toxicological) and morphological characteristics compared to other cone snails, which generally have more specialized diets.

Fossils of this species have been found in the Late Pleistocene strata of Isla Vista, California.

Californiconus was historically placed within the genus Conus but was reclassified based on its unique shell morphology and radular features, such as a lack of basal spur on its radular tooth. ficha_en: Littorina scutulata is a species of sea snail in the family Littorinidae, commonly known as periwinkles or winkles. This gastropod is found lower on rocky surfaces compared to related species such as Littorina planaxis and exhibits vertical migrations with the tides, moving up and down the rocks and exiting tide pools at night. It often hides in cracks or barnacle shells during low tide. The shell is typical of the genus Littorina, which features thick, pointed turbinated shells with a rounded aperture, flattened columella, and scarcity of whorls. The shell measures within the size range typical for Littorina species, but the Procrustes distance of 101491 indicates that Littorina scutulata's shell form is morphologically divergent from the average in its group. The snail is distributed from Kodiak Island, Alaska, to Bahia de Tortuga, Baja California, indicating a preference for colder northern and temperate waters. In feeding, Littorina scutulata primarily consumes diatom films, microscopic algae, lichens, and sometimes larger algae such as Pelvetia and Ulva. The species reproduces year-round except during summer, with eggs laid underwater in gelatinous spiral masses housing over 2000 eggs. It also harbors parasitic flukes in over 10% of individuals in regions like Oregon, while sea stars such as Leptasterias hexactis are known predators. Interestingly, its eye anatomy is comparable to land snails such as Helix aspera.

La concha es típica del género Littorina, que presenta conchas turbina gruesas y puntiagudas con una apertura redondeada, columela plana y escasez de vueltas. El caracol se distribuye desde la Isla Kodiak, Alaska, hasta Bahía de Tortuga, Baja California, indicando una preferencia por aguas frías del norte y templadas. En su alimentación, Littorina scutulata consume principalmente películas de diatomeas, microalgas, líquenes y, a veces, algas más grandes como Pelvetia y Ulva.
